decisions.reason: As an adjustable quarter-pallet display close to the core offer, it preserves a flexible low-cost option with broad customer applicability, so keeping it is justified even in a flat market.
The pegboard-back variant adds a distinct use case within the firm’s established cardboard display platform, making it a cheap and still valuable option to retain.
A standard quarter-pallet cardboard display is too close to other core variants and, after several years, its upside appears sufficiently revealed to justify pruning this redundant option.
The eighth-pallet format serves a different retail footprint while using the same established capabilities, so it remains a worthwhile low-cost option to keep open.

The wooden display pallet extends beyond the firm’s main paper-based platform and likely ties up more distinct material and production resources, so the option value no longer outweighs the cost of carrying it.
A media-specific quarter-pallet display looks like a narrower niche whose prospects should be clear by 2022, so management would reallocate resources to broader core display formats.
